headline: Approved zoning variances for projects at 276 N State St, 44 S Main St, 124 Hall Street, 16 Prince St and 148 Loudon Rd.
summary: A one-year extension was approved for a child day care special exception and variance at 76-78 S State St. Owners at 16 Prince St and 124 Hall Street also received setback and sign variances. Plans at 148 Loudon Rd call for a bank in place of the former Pizza Hut, with 18 parking spaces.
decisions: Approved a one-year extension, to November 6, 2027, for the special exception and variance at 76-78 S State St, 4-0.
Approved a determination that the agenda applications are not developments of regional impact, 4-0-0.
Approved outdoor storage variances at 276 N State St, with conditions, 4-0.
Approved sign variances at 44 S Main St, 4-0.
Conditionally approved a sign variance for placement in the public right-of-way at 44 S Main St, 4-0.
Approved sign area and freestanding sign variances at 124 Hall Street, 4-0.
Approved front yard setback variances at 16 Prince St, allowing a 1-foot setback where 10 feet is required, 4-0.
Approved a residential buffer variance at 148 Loudon Rd, 4-0.

plain_text:
November 4, 2026 
MEETING MINUTES - DRAFT 
 
Attendees: Member Nicholas Wallner, Member James Monahan, Member Andrew Winters and 
Alternate Member Ann Rice 
 
Absent: Chair Christopher Carley, Member Laura Spector-Morgan, Alternate Member Brenda 
Perkins and Alternate Member Craig Walker 
 
Staff: Kearsten O’Brien, Senior Planner and Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
  
  
 
1. Call to order 
Acting Chair Wallner called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
2. Chairperson’s comments 
Acting Chair Wallner advised the applicants tonight there is a four-member Board. The applicant has 
the right to be heard by a five-member board and asked all applicants if they wish to move to a date 
certain of December 2, 2026. Acting Chair Wallner advised all applicants that if their application is 
denied by a four-member board they will not be able to request a rehearing.  
 
All applicants agreed to be heard by a four-member Board.   
 
Acting Chair Wallner appointed Alternate Member Rice as a voting member in the place of Member 
Spector-Morgan. 
 
3. Public meetings 
• Ryan M. Dyer and Sara Dyer request an extension for the previously approved special exception for a 
child day care facility, per Section 28-2-4(j)(B) Table of Principal Uses – Educational and 
Institutional, and a variance from Section 28-7-2(e)(B) Table of Off-Street Parking Requirements, to 
allow 9 off-street parking spaces where 15 (9 for the child day care facility and 6 for the existing 
apartment units) are required, at 76-78 S State St, in the Urban Transitional (UT) District. (ZBA-
0231-2024) 
 
The consensus of the Board is that the applicant is doing a good job to keep the project on track and 
waiting on state approvals and other factors that are reasonable.  
 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Rice, seconded by Member Winters, with a vote of 4 (Rice, 
Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to granted a one-year 
extension request to the previously granted special exception and variance (ZBA 0231-2024, 
  
C I T Y  O F  C O N C O R D 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™ 
Zoning Board of Adjustment
referenced below) to expire on Novmeber 6, 2027. 
 
• Determinations of Regional Impact 
On a motion made by Member Monahan, seconded by Member Rice, the Board voted 4-0-0 to accept 
the staff recommendation to determine all of the applications on the agenda are not a development of 
regional impact, per RSA 36:55. 
 
4. Public hearings 
4.1 Allision McIntosh request the following variances on behalf of Dartnell Properties LLC: 
a) Section 28-5-37(a) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to allow outdoor storage to 
be located in the required front yards or closer than fifty (50) feet to any street or 
residential boundary line; 
b) Section 28-5-37(b) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to not require outdoor 
storage to be screened from view of adjacent properties by the installation of solid opaque 
fences, walls or enclosures; and 
c) Section 28-5-37(c) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to not require a 
landscaping buffer to be established in addition to the required screening adjacent to the 
residential boundaries. 
Located at Tax Map and Lot 58/Z 12 with an address of 276 N State St. (ZBA 0476-2026) 
(Continued from 09/02/2026) 
 
Allison McIntosh (276 N State St, Concord) has a printout of the site proposal and handed out to the 
Board. Ms. McIntosh identified area in blue which does not meet the setback requirements. The first 
area in blue does not meet the 50 feet required and is requesting a variance. This is a corner lot and 
has two frontages on North State Street and McGuire St. It does have natural landscape barriers. Ms. 
McIntosh is looking to store equipment. The third piece is the area three and they withdrew that 
request.  
 
Member Winters asked if the retaining wall will partially block the equipment.  
 
Ms. McIntosh replied yes it will be parked below the line 
 
Member Winters asked if they scaled it back 
 
Ms. McIntosh replied yes and they understand and is asking for the square section to be allowed. 
 
Alternate Member Rice asked if there are any residents.   
 
Ms. McIntosh replied yes, there are residents. Ms. McIntosh presented the building and location of 
where the equipment will be stored. 
 
Member Winters asked how they will get cars into the parking lot. 
 
Ms. McIntosh replied the parking lot is off of McGuire Street.  
 
Acting Chair Wallner asked if there is anyone that wishes to speak in favor or opposition, with none 
asked for comments from Planning.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated the variance covers the violation and site plan would be determined by staff.
Acting Chair Wallner closed the public hearing. 
 
The consensus of the Board was that the blue level and corner lot  
 
On a motion made by Member Monahan, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 4 
(Rice, Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the following 
variances located at Tax Map and Lot 58/Z 12 with an address of 276 N State St, because all of 
the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the Board and I move to adopt the 
applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.” : 
a) Section 28-5-37(a) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to allow outdoor storage to be 
located in the required front yards or closer than fifty (50) feet to any street or residential 
boundary line; 
b) Section 28-5-37(b) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to not require outdoor storage to 
be screened from view of adjacent properties by the installation of solid opaque fences, walls or 
enclosures; and 
c) Section 28-5-37(c) Outside Storage of Materials and Inventory to not require a landscaping buffer 
to be established in addition to the required screening adjacent to the residential boundaries. 
 
With the following conditions: 
1. Obtaining any applicable permitting, including site plan review if determined applicable by the 
Community Development Department; 
2. Outdoor storage limited to the blue area (about 1,478 sq ft: 43'-1" along the retaining wall, 40' at 
the addition corner, about 39' at the rear, 36' deep), as shown on the site sketch (Exhibit F). To the 
extent the Board determines relief for the pink area is necessary and grants it in addition to the 
blue area, pink area storage limited to 5' x 28' along the building (Exhibit F); 
3. Pink area of site plan, limited to small items kept within the line of the building's existing 5-foot 
front steps; 
4. No storage within the grass strips and banks along N State St and McGuire St, and no storage in 
front of the retaining wall; 
5. The existing retaining wall and grass strips and banks will be maintained in good condition; 
6. Storage limited to rental and retail equipment and products kept neat and orderly; no loose 
materials. 
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
4.2 Ari Pollack, Gallagher Callahan and Gartrell PC on behalf of Capital Center for the Arts requests the 
following variances at 44 S Main St., Tax Map and Lot 7413/Z 24 in the Central Business 
Performance (CBP) District. (ZBA 0496-2026): 
a) Section 28-6-9(a) and (b)(1), Table of Maximum Sign Dimensions for Nonresidential 
Districts and Permitted Building Signs to allow a total of five (5) building signs, 
including marquee sign panels, with a total marquee square footage of 372 square feet, 
and two building-mounted logo signs of 92 SF, for a total of 464 square feet whereas 
150 square feet is permitted and; 
b) Section 28-6-7(g), Signs Prohibited to allow signage that is located within the public 
right-of-way, whereas such placements are otherwise prohibited and; 
c) Section 28-6-7(h), Signs Prohibited to allow signage that is intermittently illuminated, 
whereas such intermittent illumination is otherwise prohibited and; 
d) Section 28-6-7(r), Signs Prohibited to allow electronic message center signage, 
whereas such messaging signs are otherwise prohibited.
Ari Pollack (214 N Main St, Concord) and Sal Prezio are present to represent this application. The 
proposed redevelopment will enclose areas of the patio and walkway. It will replace the marque sign 
and it will be fixed to the extended façade. The new sign board will display no video, automation or 
sound. The applicant has filed conceptual plans. The applicant is seeking variances for five signs and 
three are the three-sided marque. They will need a license from Concord City Council. They have 
asked for variance for intermittent illuminated during the day. The last item is an electronic message 
center which is prohibited. The proposed signs are new signs. Mr. Pollack read from the criteria 
submitted with the application materials.  
 
Acting Chair Wallner asked if there is anyone that wishes to speak in favor of this application.  
 
Pieter Hollenberg (23 Meadow St, Concord) has lived in Concord for 33 years and in favor of this 
application.  
 
Michel Herman is the owner of Gibsons and lived in concord when Capital Center of the Arts started. 
Mr. Herman is in favor of this application.  
 
Matt Lehay is resident of Concord and on the Board of CCA and in favor of this application.  
 
Sheila Vargas is a resident of Concord and serves on the board of CCA and in favor of this 
application. 
 
Acting chair Wallner asked if anyone that wants to speak in favor or opposition, with none, asked for 
comment from Planning.  
 
Acting Chair Wallner closed the public hearing. 
 
The consensus of the Board was the variances are reasonable.  
 
On a motion made by Member Winters seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 4 (Rice, 
Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the following 
variances at 44 S Main St., Tax Map and Lot 7413/Z 24 in the Central Business Performance 
(CBP) District, because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the 
Board and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”:   
 
a) Section 28-6-9(a) and (b)(1), Table of Maximum Sign Dimensions for Nonresidential Districts 
and Permitted Building Signs to allow a total of five (5) building signs, including marquee sign 
panels, with a total marquee square footage of 372 square feet, and two building-mounted logo 
signs of 92 SF, for a total of 464 square feet whereas 150 square feet is permitted; and 
b) Section 28-6-7(h), Signs Prohibited to allow signage that is intermittently illuminated, whereas 
such intermittent illumination is otherwise prohibited; and 
c) Section 28-6-7(r), Signs Prohibited to allow electronic message center signage, whereas such 
messaging signs are otherwise prohibited. 
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
On a motion made by Member Winters, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 4 (Rice, 
Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to conditionally approve the 
following variance at 44 S Main St., Tax Map and Lot 7413/Z 24 in the Central Business 
Performance (CBP) District, because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the
record before the Board and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s 
findings of fact.”:   
d) Section 28-6-7(g), Signs Prohibited to allow signage that is located within the public right-of-
way, whereas such placements are otherwise prohibited with the condition that an amended 
license with the City Council is obtained to locate the sign with in the public right of way. 
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
4.3 Michael Gallagher on behalf of Northwood Capital requests the following variances at Tax Map 88/Z 
Lot 6, 124 Hall Street located within the Industrial (IN) District. (ZBA-0497-2026 and 0499-2026): 
a) Section 28-6-9(c)(1)(c) Signs Permitted in Nonresidential Districts to allow for 90 square 
feet of sign area where 40 square feet is the maximum sign area allowed and; 
b) Section 28-6-9(c)(1) Signs Permitted in Nonresidential Districts to allow for 6 free 
standing signs where one free standing sign is permitted. 
 
Michael Gallagher (97 Eddy Rd #4, Manchester) is present to represent this application. Mr. Gallagher 
stated this is to update way finding on the property. There are no material or dimension changes. They are 
proposing a tenant directory as this property has several entrances.  
 
After taking no public testimony Acting Chair Wallner closed the public hearing.  
 
The consensus of the Board is that the property is unique and improving the way finding is beneficial. 
 
On a motion made by Member Monahan, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 4 
(Rice, Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the following 
variances at Tax Map 88/Z Lot 6, 124 Hall Street located within the Industrial (IN) District, 
because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the Board and I 
move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”:   
 
a) Section 28-6-9(c)(1)(c) Signs Permitted in Nonresidential Districts to allow for 90 square feet of 
sign area where 40 square feet is the maximum sign area allowed; and 
b) Section 28-6-9(c)(1) Signs Permitted in Nonresidential Districts to allow for 6 free standing signs 
where one free standing sign is permitted. 
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
4.4 James Murphy requests a variance from Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-
1(d)(1) Front Yard Setbacks to allow for a 1-foot front yard setback where 10 feet is required within the 
Downtown Residential (RD) District. Located at Tax Map 6444/Z Lot 75, 16 Prince St. (ZBA-0498-
2026)  
Laurie Murphy and James Murphy (16 Prince St, Concord) are present to represent this application. Ms. 
Murphy would like to have steps installed for easier access for emergency vehicles and guests. 
 
Acting Chair Wallner asked if anyone wishes to speak in favor or opposition on this application, with 
none. Acting Chair Wallner read in a letter from Mr. McNamara for the record. Then asked for comment 
from Planning 
 
Ms. O’Brien noted in the staff memo the house was built in 1830 and predates zoning.
The consensus of the Board is that the variances are reasonable.  
 
On a motion made by Alternate Member Rice, seconded by Member Winters, with a vote of 4 (Rice, 
(Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant variances from 
Sections 28-4-1(h) Table of Dimensional Requirements and 28-4-1(d)(1) Front Yard Setbacks to 
allow for a 1-foot front yard setback where 10 feet is required at Tax Map 6444/Z Lot 75, 16 Prince 
St located within the Downtown Residential (RD) District, because all of the criteria under RSA 
674:33 were met based on the record before the Board and I move to adopt the applicant’s proposed 
findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”: . 
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
4.5 Jason Hill on behalf of Wychwood Granite LLC requests a variance from Section 28-4-2 Buffer 
Requirements for Residential District Boundaries to allow for an alternative residential buffer including 
parking and driveways within the required 15-foot residential buffer. Located at Tax Map 603/Z Lot 178, 
148 Loudon Rd within the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (ZBA 0500-2026)  
 
Tom Burns (48 Constitution Dr, Bedford) is present to represent this application. Mr. Burns noted this is 
the former location of the Pizza Hut. There is an entrance off Canterbury Road and Loudon Road. The 
site has 44 parking spaces. The applicant is proposing to remove the Pizza Hut and build a bank in the 
middle of the lot. They will keep the entrance off Canterbury Road and eliminate the entrance on Loudon 
Road to make it a right out exit only for safety. They will reduce the parking to 18 spaces. They are 
adding green space that will improve the site. There is a 15-foot buffer for residential. Mr. Burns read 
from the criteria submitted with the application materials.  
 
On a motion made by Member Winters, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, with a vote of 4 (Rice, 
Winters, Wallner and Monahan) in favor to 0 opposed, the Board voted to grant the variance from 
Section 28-4-2 Buffer Requirements for Residential District Boundaries to allow for an alternative 
residential buffer including parking and driveways within the required 15-foot residential buffer at 
Tax Map 603/Z Lot 178, 148 Loudon Rd within the Gateway Performance (GWP) District, 
because all of the criteria under RSA 674:33 were met based on the record before the Board and I 
move to adopt the applicant’s proposed findings as the Board’s findings of fact.”:   
 
The adopted Findings of Fact are on file with the Planning Division of the Community Development 
Department. 
 
5. Review and acceptance of minutes from October 7, 2026 
Alternate Member Rice moved, seconded by Member Winters, to approve the meeting minutes from 
October 7, 2026, as written. The Board voted 4 in favor (Rice, Winters, Wallner and Monahan) to 0 
opposed. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
6. Any other business that may legally come before the Zoning Board 
None. 
 
7. Adjourn 
On a motion made by Member Monahan, seconded by Alternate Member Rice, the Board voted 4 in favor 
to 0 opposed to adjourn at 7:58 p.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted,
Krista Tremblay 
Krista Tremblay 
Administrative Technician III
